sources: Siptár, P., & Törkenczy, M. (2000). The Phonology of Hungarian. Oxford University Press. https://global.oup.com/academic/product/the-phonology-of-hungarian-9780198238416
preamble: Palatalization of the alveolar stop [t] to the palatal stop [c] before a palatal glide or front vowel. In Hungarian /t/ + /j/ fully assimilates to [cː] (látja), and Czech softening turns /t/ into /c/ (ť) before i/í and ě.

examples.note: Obligatory full palatal assimilation of t + j.
Optional partial assimilation before a palatal stop.
Hard t is softened to palatal ť /c/ before i; spelled ⟨ti⟩.
